newsitem.title: CHINA: China not seen listing legal person shares soon.
newsitem.headline: China not seen listing legal person shares soon.

text.p: China is not likely to list legal person shares and non-tradable rights shares in the near future, though their impact on local stock markets would be limited if issues were well paced, analysts said on Tuesday.

Many state companies list a small portion of their shares, with the remainder -- the so-called legal person shares -- held by official organisations such as state enterprises, institutions and government bodies, the analysts said.
This was designed to ensure continued state control over these companies after listing, they said.
Legal person shares were not tradable on China's two stock exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen and rights issues to legal person shareholders were also banned from listing, they said.
An official with China's Securities Regulatory Commission told Reuters that China was considering allowing non-tradable shares to list as part of a long-term plan to reform state-owned enterprises.
But he said he was unaware of any imminent announcement.
"Even if these shares are allowed to be listed, the impact will be more psychological as the volume is thin against total stock capitalisation," a local broker said.

Brokers estimated that with rights issues of legal person shares numbering one to 1.5 billion, their listing would absorb up to 20 billion yuan or only around five percent of the total A share market capitalisation.

Over the past few years, many legal person shareholders in need of funds had given up the option to subscribe to rights issues, selling the option instead to private shareholders for between 0.1 yuan to one yuan per rights share, analysts said.

"The possibility of allowing legal person shares to go public this year is small as the listing of these shares may have an impact on the goverment control over these key state-owned companies," said an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage.
So far, China has issued 137.149 billion domestic currency shares valued at 1,490.44 billion yuan ($179.57 billion), official statistics show.
Of this figure, 100.578 billion shares worth 1,068.439 billion yuan are owned by legal person shareholders and rights issues originally offered to legal person shareholders, the statistics show.
Analysts said rights issues of legal person shares were more likely to be listed than the legal person shares themselves.
Rights shares would most probably go public at a measured pace and in a limited volume, some said.
"Beijing is very likely to allow the listing (of rights shares) this year as a new measure to fight excessive stock speculation," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Recent market rumours said Beijing would allow non-tradable rights issues to be listed to help boost liquidity and curb speculation.

"I do not think this will happen this year as the government has announced enough quota for issuing new shares if they want to curb over-speculation by means of quick market expansion," said an analyst with a major brokerage in Shanghai.
